close_reason: Replaced parse_address_list and extract_msg_ids in MemoryBackend with mime-tree-delegating helpers parse_address_list_via_mime_tree and parse_msg_ids_via_mime_tree at memory.rs:1945. Email/get .from/.to/.cc properties now parse through the same mime-tree gateway as header:<name>:asAddresses, so the encoded-word / quoted-comma / group cases that previously diverged now agree. New integration test email_get_from_property_matches_as_addresses asserts the equivalence on an input exercising both edge cases. mime-tree was already a hard runtime dep (commit e99c3dc); no new dependency. 253 mail-server tests pass (was 252).
description:
MemoryBackend has two distinct paths that both parse RFC 5322 address-list headers:

1. memory.rs:1827 parse_address_list — hand-rolled simple parser used by parse_rfc5322_headers during Email/import and Email/copy. Output goes into email.from / .to / .cc which clients see on a plain Email/get request for the 'from' property.

2. email.rs:307 apply_header_form (As*) — uses mime_tree::parse_header_typed (mail-parser underneath) when a client requests 'header:From:asAddresses' or :asGroupedAddresses.

These parsers have different behaviour on identical input:

- RFC 2047 encoded-words: mime-tree decodes (=?UTF-8?Q?John_Sm=C3=AEth?= → John Smîth); parse_address_list keeps the literal encoded-word as the display name.
- RFC 5322 groups: mime-tree handles 'Friends: a@x, b@y;' as a group structure; parse_address_list splits on commas inside the group, producing mangled output.
- Quoted-strings with commas in display names: 'Smith, John' <a@x> → mime-tree treats as one mailbox; parse_address_list splits on the comma, getting two malformed entries.

Net result: in MemoryBackend, the JMAP 'from' property and the 'header:From:asAddresses' property can return semantically different values for the same email. The RFC 8621 spec says both forms parse the same Address-list grammar — a conforming server should produce equivalent results.

This is a MemoryBackend reference-impl simplification, explicitly acknowledged by the parse_rfc5322_headers doc comment (memory.rs:1703-1704: 'intentionally simple — it handles the common cases in tests. A production implementation would use a proper MIME library.'). So this is not a wire-protocol bug in the published mail-server crate — production backends are expected to use a proper parser for both paths.

But for the workspace tests, this means tests that compare 'from' values against 'header:From:asAddresses' on real-world inputs will see false discrepancies blamed on the As* path. The workspace test suite currently dodges this by using RFC-grade simple inputs in both code paths; if a future test stitches them together against more complex fixtures, the inconsistency will surface as a test failure that looks like a bug in As* when it's actually parse_address_list misbehaving.

Two options for the reference impl:

a. Route parse_rfc5322_headers' address-extraction through mime-tree too — single source of truth, behavioural alignment with As*. mime-tree is now a hard dep of mail-server (e99c3dc), so the cost is zero.

b. Document the divergence explicitly in memory.rs:1703 and add a test that asserts the known mismatch on a fixture with encoded-words, so future surprise is visible.

Option (a) is the better engineering call now that mime-tree is mandatory. The parse_address_list / extract_msg_ids functions in memory.rs become dead code and can be removed.
title: MemoryBackend uses two different address parsers (Email/get from vs As*)
